As, it is a logarithmic function : $x^2\ne\ 0\ $ .
Let's verify now $x^2=3$ : 
$\log\left(3-10^{\displaystyle\log x^2}\right)\ =\ \log\left(3-x^2\right)$
This implies, $x^2\ne\ 3\ $

Due to spoilage, he was able to sell only 50% of the apples at a 20% profit and only ${\dfrac{2}{3}}^{^\text{rd}}$ of the mangoes at a 30% profit. Let the cost price of each fruit be $X$. 
So, the total cost to the seller = $30X$
It is also given that he had incurred a total loss of ₹880:  $30(X)- \text{ loss amount }= \text{ Revenue}$
Where the revenue is given as ₹2120. 
                                  
So,  $30(X)-880=2120$  or  $X=\dfrac{2120+880}{30}$
We get $X=₹100$, which will be the cost price of each fruit. 
Given that 50% apples are sold at 20% profit & $\dfrac{2}{3}$rd mangoes are sold at 30% profit: 
$\left(1.2\times \dfrac{a}{2}\times X\right) + \left(1.3\times \dfrac{2(30-a)}{3}\times X \right)=2120$
Putting $X=100$, we get
$\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\times 120\right)+\left( \dfrac{(60-2a)}{3}\times 130\right)=2120$
$60a+2600 - \dfrac{260a}{3}=2120$
$\dfrac{80a}{3} = 480$  or  $a=18$
Therefore, the revenue he got by selling apples = $\dfrac{18}{2}\times 120=1080$

questions.question_text: Find the area (in units square) of the region bounded by $∣x∣+∣x\ −\ y∣\le8$.
questions.solution_text:
First, we have to find the boundary points. So, we will assume the equation is equal to 8 to make calculations simpler.
Case 1: $x\ge0$ and  $x-y\ge0$
In this case, the equation becomes: $x+(x−y)=8$
$2x−y=8$ or $y=2x-8$
Case 2: $x\ge0$ and $x−y<0$
In this case, the equation becomes: x-(x−y)=8
$y=8$ and $x=0$
Case 3: $x<0$ and $x−y\ge0$
In this case, the equation becomes:−x+(x−y)=8
$y=−8$ and $x=0$
Case 4: $x<0$ & $x−y<0$
In this case, the equation becomes: $−x−(x−y)=8$
$-2x+y=8$ or $y=2x+8$
Now, let's find the intersection points:
1. $y=8$ intersects $y=2x-8$ at: $8=2x-8$
$x=8$ and $y=8$
2. $y=8$ intersects $y=2x+8$: $8=2x+8$
$x=0$ and $y=8$
3.$y=-8$ intersects $y=2x-8$:$-8=2x-8$
$x=0$ and $y=-8$
4. $y=-8$ intersects $y=2x+8:-8=2x+8$
$x=-8$ and $y=-8$
Hence, we get the coordinates as (8,8), (0,8), (0,-8) and (-8,-8), and the figure will be of the shape of a parallelogram. 
We need to find the area of the parallelogram. The base of the parallelogram will be of 8 units and the height will be 16 units.
Area of the parallelogram = Base*Height = 8*16 = 128 units square.

Let $D_n$ represent the absolute difference between the interests earned by both of them in the $n^{th}$ year. If $\dfrac{\ D_3}{D_2}$ = $\dfrac{\ a}{b}$, such that $a$ & $b$ are co-primes. Then find the value of $|a-b|$ .
questions.solution_text:
Pranjal : $P_1=10,000$ , $R_1=\ 20\%$  compounding .
Naseeb : $P_2=20,000$ , $R_1=\ 10\%$  simple interest.
In $3^{rd}$ year : 
1. Interest earned by Pranjal = $P_1\left(1+\frac{\ R_1}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{\ R_1}{100}\right)$
                                            =  $10,000\left(1+\frac{\ 20}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{\ 20}{100}\right)$
                                            =  $80\times36$ 
                                            =  $2880$
2. Interest earned by Naseeb = $\dfrac{\ P_2R_2\left(1\right)}{100}$ = $\dfrac{\ 20000\times10}{100}=2000$
Hence, the value of $D_3=\left|2880-2000\right|=880$
In $2^{nd}$ year : 
1.   Interest earned by Pranjal = $P_1\left(1+\frac{\ R_1}{100}\right)^1\left(\frac{\ R_1}{100}\right)$
                                              = $10,000\left(1+\frac{\ 20}{100}\right)^1\left(\frac{\ 20}{100}\right)$
                                              = $400\times6$
                                              = 2400
2. Interest earned by Naseeb = $\dfrac{\ P_2R_2\left(1\right)}{100}$ = $\dfrac{\ 20000\times10}{100}=2000$
Hence, the value of $D_2=\left|2400-2000\right|=400$
Therefore, $\dfrac{\ D_3}{D_2}$ = $\dfrac{\ 880}{400}$ = $\dfrac{\ 11}{5}$ 
Therefore, the value of $|a-b|=|11-5|=6$ .

Container A contains a mixture of milk and water in some unknown ratio. This mixture is combined with another solution B of 20 litres that contains 25% milk. The resulting mixture has a 30% milk concentration. If instead, the same mixture A is mixed with 10 litres of pure milk, the resulting mixture has a 40% milk concentration.

Find the initial quantity of milk present in mixture A.
questions.solution_text:
Let the total volume of mixture A be $"V"$ and the concentration of milk be $"a\ \%"$ in it .
Mixture A + Solution B (25% milk in 20 litre) : Resulting solution has 30% milk
Milk :  $\dfrac{\ a}{100}\left(V\right)+\dfrac{\ 25}{100}\left(20\right)=\dfrac{\ 30}{100}\left(V+20\right)$
           
                         $\dfrac{\ a\left(V\right)}{100}=\dfrac{\ 3V}{10}+1$ $\rightarrow$ Eq(1)
Mixture A + 10 litre milk : Resulting solution has 40% milk 
Milk :  $\dfrac{\ a\left(V\right)}{100}+10\ =\dfrac{\ 40}{100}\left(V+10\right)$
                       $\dfrac{\ a\left(V\right)}{100}+6\ =\dfrac{\ 4V}{10}$ $\rightarrow$ Eq(2)
By solving, Eq(1) & Eq(2) : $V=70\ L$
Therefore, the initial quantity of milk present in mixture A $=\dfrac{\ a\left(V\right)}{100}=\left(\dfrac{\ 3\left(70\right)}{10}+1\right)\ =22\ litres$

questions.question_text: A can complete a piece of work in 6 days, B in 10 days, and C in 12 days. If B and C work on alternate days, while A works every third day, and C starts the work alone on the first day, followed by B on the second day and A on the third day, then on which day will the work be completed?
questions.solution_text:
Let the total work done be 60 units. 
A can complete a piece of work in 6 days, B in 10 days, and C in 12 days. Thus, the efficiency of A will be 10 units/day, the efficiency of B will be 6 units/day, and the efficiency of C will be 5 units/day. 
C starts the work alone on the first day, B begins on the second day, and A begins on the third day. Also, B and C work on alternate days, while A works every third day. 
So, A is working on the day which is a multiple of 3, B is working on every even-numbered day, and C is working on every odd-numbered day. 
As per their efficiency, the work done by each by the end of 6 days will be - 
A = __ __ 10 __ __ 10 = 20 units  
B = __ 6 __ 6 __ 6 = 18 units
C = 5 __ 5 __ 5 __ = 15 units
Thus, 53 units of work are done uptil the 6th day. On the seventh day, only C will be working and thus (53 + 5 = 58) units of work will be completed by the seventh day. On the eighth day, only B will be working, thus the entire work will be completed. 
Therefore, the work will be completed on the 8th day.

questions.question_text: Two ships A and B have to do a round trip to an island 1 km away. The average speed calculated for boat A is 3.2 km/hr and for boat B is 1.75 km/hr. If the speed of stream is 3 km/hr, find the ratio of speeds of ship B and ship A.
questions.solution_text:
Let's find a general expression for average time for a boat completing a round trip.
Let speed of boat be b, speed of stream be s, distance of island from port be D
Also lets assume that ongoing trip will be upstream so return trip will be downstream.
So time for ongoing journey (upstream) $=\dfrac{D}{b-s}$
TIme for return journey (downstream) $=\dfrac{D}{b+s}$
Now, $\text{Average Speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}}$
or, average speed = $\dfrac{D+D}{\dfrac{D}{b-s}+\dfrac{D}{b+s}}$
or, average speed = $\dfrac{D+D}{D\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{b-s}+\dfrac{1}{b+s}\right)}$
or, average speed = $\dfrac{2D}{D\cdot\left(\dfrac{2b}{b^2-s^2}\right)}$
or, average speed = $\dfrac{b^2-s^2}{b}$
Now let speed of boat 1 be b1 and boat of speed 2 be b2.
So, $\dfrac{\left(b1\right)^2-s^2}{\left(b1\right)}$
=> $\dfrac{\left(b1^2-3^2\right)}{b1}=3.2$
=>$\dfrac{\left(b1^2-3^2\right)}{b1}=\dfrac{16}{5}$ 
(Since, 3.2 was given, to make calculations easy we can convert it to dfraction form 16/5)
Upon solving we get b1 as  5 km/hr.
Similarly, $\dfrac{\left(\left(b2\right)^2-3^2\right)}{b2}=1.75$
=>$\dfrac{\left(\left(b2\right)^2-3^2\right)}{b2}=\dfrac{7}{4}$
(Since, 1.75 was given, to make calculations easy we can convert it to fraction form 7/4)
Upon solving we get b2 as 4 km/hr.
So, ratio of speed of ship B and ship A is 4:5 = 0.8
Option A.

Squaring both sides

$\frac{b^2}{a^2}-\frac{4c}{a}=16$
Since $a \ne 0$ Cross-multiplying $a^2$
$b^2-4ca=16a^2$
$b^2-16a^2=4ca$
$\left(b+4a\right)\left(b-4a\right)=4ca$
The roots are non zero. Hence c is not zero. So none of the terms in the above products are zero.
On re-arranging we get $\frac{b+4a}{4c}=\frac{a}{b-4a}$

questions.question_text: A group of four women and five men are to be arranged in a straight line. Let $Q$ represent the number of possible arrangements in which all four women stand together, and let $P$ represent the number of possible arrangements in which exactly four men stand together. Find the value of $\dfrac{3P}{Q}$.
questions.solution_text:
$Q$ is the number of ways in which all four women stand together.
The four women standing together can do so in $4!$ ways and form a group. This group, along with five other men, form a group having a total of $5+1=6$ entities. The number of ways of arranging these entities will be $6!$. Therefore, the total number of ways of arranging the people such that all four women stand together is $4!\times 6! =Q$.
$P$ is the number of ways in which exactly four men stand together.
Consider a group of four men that can be arranged internally in $4!$ ways. This group, along with one remaining man and the four women, are a total of $6$ entities and can be arranged in $6!$ ways. The total number of ways, therefore, are $4!\times 6!$. We must remove cases where the remaining man sits adjacent to the group of four men. This can happen in $2\times 4!\times 5!$ ways (where the all-man group and the four women form a total of five entities).
Thus, the total cases would be $6!\times 4! - 2\times 4!\times 5! = 4!\times 480$
There are a total of ${}^5C_4=5$ ways of choosing this group.
Therefore, the value of $P$ is $(5! \times 480)$.
We are to calculate $\dfrac{3P}{Q}$
$\dfrac{3P}{Q} = 3\times \dfrac{5! \times 480}{4!\times 6!} = 3\times  \dfrac{480}{6\times 24}= 10$

Four boxes contain 12 balls each. The number of red balls in the boxes is

A box is chosen at random, and then a ball is picked at random from that box.

Since a box is chosen at random,
P(B1) = P(B2) = P(B3) = P(B4) = $\dfrac{1}{4}$
The probability of picking a red ball given a particular box is
$P\left(\dfrac{R}{B1}\right)=\dfrac{4}{12}$

$P\left(\dfrac{R}{B3}\right)=\dfrac{6}{12}$
$P\left(\dfrac{R}{B4}\right)=\dfrac{7}{12}$

$P\left(R\right)$ = $\dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{4}{12}+\dfrac{5}{12}+\dfrac{6}{12}+\dfrac{7}{12}\right]=\dfrac{11}{24}$

questions.question_text: By joining the midpoints of its sides of a regular hexagon, a new hexagon is formed. The same process is repeated on each newly formed hexagon. If the total area of all these hexagons is $216\sqrt{3}\ cm^2$, then what is the length of the longest diagonal of the original hexagon (in cm)?
questions.solution_text:
Let the length of the regular hexagon be a cm. BC is the length of the new hexagon, which is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of the original hexagon. 
Applying the cosine rule in $\triangle ABC$ - 
$\cos120^{\circ}=\dfrac{\left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2-BC^2}{2\times\frac{a}{2}\times\frac{a}{2}}$
$-\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2-BC^2$
$BC=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{2}$
Now, the midpoints of this new hexagon are joined together to form another hexagon. The side of this new hexagon will be $=BC\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\dfrac{3a}{4}$. This process will continue for all the newly formed hexagons. 
Area of hexagon = $\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\times Side^2$ 
Sum of areas of hexagons $=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}a^2}{2}+\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{2}\right)^2}{2}+\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{3a}{4}\right)^2}{2}+....$
$216\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\left[a^2+\dfrac{3a^2}{4}+\dfrac{9a^2}{16}+...\right]$
$216\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\left[\dfrac{a^2}{1-\frac{3}{4}}\right]$
$108\sqrt{3}=3\sqrt{3}a^2$
$a=6\ cm$
Length of the longest diagonal of the original hexagon = $2a=12$ cm.

All three — A, B, and C — start working together on the project, but after 4 days C leaves. Determine the minimum total number of days required to finish the project.

Let the total work be $W$ units.
As A alone would have finished the work in 20 days: $(\text{Efficiency of A})\times 20=W$ or $E_A=\dfrac{W}{20}$
Efficiency of B is half that of A: $E_B=\dfrac{1}{2}\times \dfrac{W}{20} =\dfrac{W}{40}$ 
Efficiency of C is twice that of B: $E_c= 2\times \dfrac{W}{40}=\dfrac{W}{20}$
For the first 4 days: A, B, C worked together:
Amount of work done in first 4 days $=\left(\dfrac{W}{20}+\dfrac{W}{40}+\dfrac{W}{20}\right)\times 4 =\dfrac{W}{2}$.
For the next "t" days: Only A & B worked together: 
Remaining work to be done $\Rightarrow \dfrac{W}{2}=\left(\dfrac{W}{20}+\dfrac{W}{40}\right)\times t$
From this, we get: $t=\dfrac{20}{3}$ days
Therefore, total days it takes to finish the project $=\ 4 +\dfrac{20}{3}=10.66$ days
Hence, the total minimum number of days required to finish the project is 11.

He first removed the same amount of water, $K$ litres from each, then interchanged it, such that the price per litre for the two mixtures is now the same.What is the value of $13K$?
questions.solution_text:
Let the bisleri water be priced at Rs $b$ per liter, and the himalaya water is Rs $h$ per litre. Also, $K$ litres of water is interchanged initially. Raman has 8 litres of Bisleri and 5 litres of Himalaya water.
We are told that after interchanging the waters, the cost per litre for both is same.
i.e, $\ \dfrac{(8-K)b+Kh}{8}=\dfrac{(5-K)h+Kb}{5}$
or, $\ 5[(8-K)b+Kh]=8[(5-K)h+Kb]$
or, $\ 40b-5Kb+5Kh=40h-8Kh+8Kb$
or, $\ 40\left(b-h\right)=13K\left(b-h\right)$
or, $\ K=\dfrac{40}{13}$ litres 
so, $\ 13K=40$
